elements.element: Preferred: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "by giving not less than 90 days' prior notice, in writing" — 90 days, not 30

elements.element: Preferred: pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer termination
elements.evidence: no refund language; instead "any early-termination fee payable by Customer ... shall not exceed three (3) months' fees"

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term" (a right is granted, albeit end-of-term only)

elements.element: Fallback: Customer termination for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period, by giving not less than 90 days' prior notice, in writing"

elements.element: Fallback: early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "any early-termination fee payable by Customer by reason of such termination shall not exceed three (3) months' fees"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination only effective at end of a term
elements.evidence: "Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "on not less than 90 days' prior written notice"

reasons: All three fallback elements are expressly present: Customer convenience exit on 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 day band), an early-termination fee cap of three months' fees, and Vendor's convenience right confined to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice.

Preferred is not met (notice is 90 rather than 30 days, there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and Vendor retains an end-of-term convenience right), which is consistent with the locked fallback target.

Minimality holds: a single concise inserted paragraph supplies a right that was wholly absent (the original permitted exit during the Initial Period only by unanimous agreement); the phrase 'including during the Initial Period' is necessary to override that bar rather than surplus.

Intent is preserved: 18.1, 18.2 and the capital-cost proviso remain effective and no undefined term is introduced. Minor point to watch: Vendor's new 90-day end-of-term notice sits alongside 18.1's one (1) year notice for any Party, so it may be worth stating the new sentence is without prejudice to the longer notice in 18.1.
